Czarny Dunajec Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Czarny Dunajec, Poland

Not demolished. Czarny Dunajec's Jewish community, settled from the second half of the 19th century, numbered 405 people (14 percent of the town) by 1939; rather than a local ghetto, Jews here were systematically transported to the Nowy Targ Ghetto, and a 1942 forced labor camp gathered about 90 more before their deportation to Bełżec. This cemetery was almost completely destroyed during WWII, its tombstones used to pave streets, and was the site of numerous German executions. In 2020, the Popiel Family Foundation, in cooperation with the Nissenbaum Family Foundation, fenced the site and erected a central monument listing 494 named Holocaust victims, alongside monuments on four identified and marked mass graves.
